Dover Motor Speedway.name: Dover Motor Speedway
Dover Motor Speedway.preferredLine: Start with the lower groove and a smooth center; try a higher lane if rubber and traffic make it faster over several laps.
Dover Motor Speedway.savingGuidance: Ease entry speed and unwind the steering before applying full throttle. Protect the right front over the compressed 3× stint.
Dover Motor Speedway.watchFor: Concrete grip can change through a run. Judge a line by average stint pace, not one quick lap.
Dover Motor Speedway.referenceNote: Based on the 2025 400-lap points race; the 2026 All-Star format is different. Confirm NASCAR 26 lap count.

Daytona International Speedway.name: Daytona International Speedway
Daytona International Speedway.preferredLine: Hold the lane with the strongest organized draft; momentum and connected cars matter more than a fixed low or high groove.
Daytona International Speedway.savingGuidance: Stay tucked into a stable draft and make small throttle reductions. Do not lose the pack to chase a fuel number.
Daytona International Speedway.watchFor: Avoid sudden checks when saving. Announce coordinated pit entry and avoid crossing a moving lane.
Daytona International Speedway.referenceNote: Real-world reference; 50% lap estimate may differ from the game. Confirm the in-game race length and layout.

Charlotte Motor Speedway.name: Charlotte Motor Speedway
Charlotte Motor Speedway.preferredLine: Compare lower-to-middle grip with a higher momentum lane as the track changes. Favor the arc that holds its pace at the end of a 3× stint.
Charlotte Motor Speedway.savingGuidance: Make small earlier lifts, reduce steering scrub, and protect exit traction. Recalculate both ranges after each planned stage break.
Charlotte Motor Speedway.watchFor: The 400-lap reference is the Coca-Cola 600. The other oval event is 267 laps. BRL uses three scoring stages here; do not assume real NASCAR stage-ending laps.
Charlotte Motor Speedway.referenceNote: 400-lap reference → approximately 200 laps at 50%. Confirm the selected game event.

Nashville Superspeedway.name: Nashville Superspeedway
Nashville Superspeedway.preferredLine: Start with a consistent lower-to-middle arc. Test a higher lane as the surface changes instead of forcing a tight car down to the bottom.
Nashville Superspeedway.savingGuidance: Lift before entry and avoid scrubbing the front tires in the center. Use progressive throttle to protect rear grip.
Nashville Superspeedway.watchFor: Avoid using braking to compensate for excessive entry speed throughout a 3× tire stint.
Nashville Superspeedway.referenceNote: Real-world reference; 50% lap estimate may differ from the game. Confirm the in-game race length and layout.

Pocono Raceway.name: Pocono Raceway
Pocono Raceway.preferredLine: Use a different approach for each of the three turns. Protect the last corner exit because it leads onto the longest straight.
Pocono Raceway.savingGuidance: Lift earlier into the heavier braking zones while preserving exit speed. Check whether saving actually avoids a stop in the shortened race.
Pocono Raceway.watchFor: Three different corners create a compromise; a one-corner setup or line can lose more time elsewhere.
Pocono Raceway.referenceNote: Real-world reference; 50% lap estimate may differ from the game. Confirm the in-game race length and layout.

Bristol Motor Speedway.name: Bristol Motor Speedway
Bristol Motor Speedway.preferredLine: Compare the lower groove with the upper lane as rubber develops. The fastest lane may migrate through the run.
Bristol Motor Speedway.savingGuidance: Keep the arc smooth and avoid scrubbing the right front. Save subtly so nearby cars can anticipate your pace.
Bristol Motor Speedway.watchFor: Short laps compress decision time at 3×; plan pit entry early and confirm the front/back pit-road rules in-game.
Bristol Motor Speedway.referenceNote: Real-world reference; 50% lap estimate may differ from the game. Confirm the in-game race length and layout.

Las Vegas Motor Speedway.name: Las Vegas Motor Speedway
Las Vegas Motor Speedway.preferredLine: Test low-to-middle early and compare a higher momentum lane as grip and tire balance change.
Las Vegas Motor Speedway.savingGuidance: Make a small earlier lift and keep the arc smooth. Save without repeatedly correcting the car on exit.
Las Vegas Motor Speedway.watchFor: Pitting early only helps if fresh-tire gains beat pit loss and you have enough laps to use them.
Las Vegas Motor Speedway.referenceNote: Real-world reference; 50% lap estimate may differ from the game. Confirm the in-game race length and layout.

Talladega Superspeedway.name: Talladega Superspeedway
Talladega Superspeedway.preferredLine: Choose the best-supported drafting lane and stay connected. A passing lane needs help to remain fast.
Talladega Superspeedway.savingGuidance: Make small throttle reductions in the draft and coordinate stops. Avoid lifting abruptly in front of another car.
Talladega Superspeedway.watchFor: Saving too hard can disconnect you from the pack, making a theoretical fuel advantage irrelevant.
Talladega Superspeedway.referenceNote: Real-world reference; 50% lap estimate may differ from the game. Confirm the in-game race length and layout.

North Wilkesboro Speedway.name: North Wilkesboro Speedway
North Wilkesboro Speedway.preferredLine: Start with a low, rounded arc and compare a lane higher as grip develops. Prioritize a settled rear end on exit.
North Wilkesboro Speedway.savingGuidance: Lift earlier and roll through the center; abrupt braking and spinning the rear tires can waste the fuel and grip you are trying to save.
North Wilkesboro Speedway.watchFor: Track position matters. A tire stop must recover its pit-road loss over the remaining laps.
North Wilkesboro Speedway.referenceNote: Real-world reference; 50% lap estimate may differ from the game. Confirm the in-game race length and layout.

Indianapolis Motor Speedway.name: Indianapolis Motor Speedway
Indianapolis Motor Speedway.preferredLine: Keep a precise, consistent arc through each flat corner and prioritize clean air plus the exit onto the straights.
Indianapolis Motor Speedway.savingGuidance: Use earlier lift into the turns while avoiding a large exit-speed loss. Small repeated gains can matter over a long lap.
Indianapolis Motor Speedway.watchFor: Track position is valuable; saving is worthwhile when it prevents a stop or improves the final pit cycle.
Indianapolis Motor Speedway.referenceNote: Real-world reference; 50% lap estimate may differ from the game. Confirm the in-game race length and layout.

Phoenix Raceway.name: Phoenix Raceway
Phoenix Raceway.preferredLine: Use a smooth lower-to-middle corner arc. Confirm the league rules for the dogleg and restart boundaries.
Phoenix Raceway.savingGuidance: Back up entry, keep the car rotating, and apply throttle progressively to limit rear-wheel spin.
Phoenix Raceway.watchFor: Evaluate track position against tire advantage before giving up a restart position.
Phoenix Raceway.referenceNote: Real-world reference; 50% lap estimate may differ from the game. Confirm the in-game race length and layout.

Richmond Raceway.name: Richmond Raceway
Richmond Raceway.preferredLine: Start low with a patient entry and clean exit. Move your arc if the rear tires lose drive or the bottom stops rotating.
Richmond Raceway.savingGuidance: Earlier lift and gentle throttle application can protect both fuel and rear grip. Avoid trying to recover all the saved time at corner exit.
Richmond Raceway.watchFor: Compare tire falloff with green-flag pit loss before choosing an extra stop.
Richmond Raceway.referenceNote: Real-world reference; 50% lap estimate may differ from the game. Confirm the in-game race length and layout.

Kansas Speedway.name: Kansas Speedway
Kansas Speedway.preferredLine: Compare the middle and upper grooves for momentum; use the lower lane when it offers a clear passing opportunity.
Kansas Speedway.savingGuidance: Reduce entry speed slightly and keep steering smooth. Compare the extra distance of the high line with the fuel saved by carrying speed.
Kansas Speedway.watchFor: A high line is not automatically a fuel-saving line. Compare fuel per lap and average pace at 3×.
Kansas Speedway.referenceNote: Real-world reference; 50% lap estimate may differ from the game. Confirm the in-game race length and layout.

Texas Motor Speedway.name: Texas Motor Speedway
Texas Motor Speedway.preferredLine: Treat the two ends separately: a patient entry at one end may support a wider momentum arc at the other.
Texas Motor Speedway.savingGuidance: Lift before the car begins to push and protect the exit. Do not use extra steering to force a line that the tires can no longer hold.
Texas Motor Speedway.watchFor: With 3× wear, a line that needs fewer corrections may beat a faster qualifying arc over the stint.
Texas Motor Speedway.referenceNote: Real-world reference; 50% lap estimate may differ from the game. Confirm the in-game race length and layout.

Homestead-Miami Speedway.name: Homestead-Miami Speedway
Homestead-Miami Speedway.preferredLine: Compare the high momentum groove with a lower, shorter line. Leave a safe wall margin and judge the last laps of the stint.
Homestead-Miami Speedway.savingGuidance: Protect tire life from lap one. Smooth entry and throttle can preserve pace, but extra distance up high may offset fuel savings.
Homestead-Miami Speedway.watchFor: With 3× tire wear, a fuel-only strategy may lose to a tire-focused stop. Compare both constraints.
Homestead-Miami Speedway.referenceNote: Real-world reference; 50% lap estimate may differ from the game. Confirm the in-game race length and layout.

Atlanta - Echopark Speedway.name: Atlanta - Echopark Speedway
Atlanta - Echopark Speedway.preferredLine: Follow the most coordinated drafting lane. Choose a groove that keeps you connected rather than making repeated solo lane changes.
Atlanta - Echopark Speedway.savingGuidance: Use the draft to reduce throttle gently; judge saving against the risk of losing the pack.
Atlanta - Echopark Speedway.watchFor: The real-world pit route uses separate 90 and 45 mph zones. Confirm the game enforcement points and limits before race night.
Atlanta - Echopark Speedway.referenceNote: Real-world reference; 50% lap estimate may differ from the game. Confirm the in-game race length and layout.

Sonoma Raceway.name: Sonoma Raceway
Sonoma Raceway.preferredLine: Use a late apex where it improves acceleration onto the next straight; prioritize exit speed over deep braking.
Sonoma Raceway.savingGuidance: Lift before heavy braking zones and shorten full-throttle time without compromising a safe exit. Coast while staying on a predictable line.
Sonoma Raceway.watchFor: Rear-wheel spin and curb strikes can erase any benefit from saving fuel.
Sonoma Raceway.referenceNote: Real-world reference; 50% lap estimate may differ from the game. Confirm the in-game race length and layout.

Qualcomm Circuit at Naval Base Coronado.name: Qualcomm Circuit at Naval Base Coronado
Qualcomm Circuit at Naval Base Coronado.preferredLine: Build the lap around clean braking and exits; use conservative curb approaches until practice confirms grip.
Qualcomm Circuit at Naval Base Coronado.savingGuidance: Coast ahead of the larger braking zones while keeping entry predictable. Favor clean exits over aggressive throttle spikes.
Qualcomm Circuit at Naval Base Coronado.watchFor: Walls and narrow sections reduce recovery options. Treat this as a new-course guide to validate in practice.
Qualcomm Circuit at Naval Base Coronado.referenceNote: Real-world reference; 50% lap estimate may differ from the game. Confirm the in-game race length and layout.

Watkins Glen International.name: Watkins Glen International
Watkins Glen International.preferredLine: Prioritize clean exits and a settled car through the Esses and bus stop. Test curb usage rather than assuming every curb is faster.
Watkins Glen International.savingGuidance: Lift before heavy braking and stay smooth through direction changes; do not sacrifice exit speed onto the long straights unnecessarily.
Watkins Glen International.watchFor: Pit timing can determine track position. Do not import real NASCAR stage-caution rules into the league plan.
Watkins Glen International.referenceNote: Real-world reference; 50% lap estimate may differ from the game. Confirm the in-game race length and layout.

Chicagoland Speedway.name: Chicagoland Speedway
Chicagoland Speedway.preferredLine: Compare a lower, shorter route with a higher momentum arc. Let long-run grip decide rather than committing to one lane.
Chicagoland Speedway.savingGuidance: Reduce front-tire scrub and throttle spikes. Compare your final stint laps as well as the opening laps.
Chicagoland Speedway.watchFor: At 3×, a short qualifying advantage may disappear before the pit window.
Chicagoland Speedway.referenceNote: Real-world reference; 50% lap estimate may differ from the game. Confirm the in-game race length and layout.

Darlington Raceway.name: Darlington Raceway
Darlington Raceway.preferredLine: Test the higher momentum line with a safe wall margin; treat the two ends differently and avoid pinching the exit.
Darlington Raceway.savingGuidance: Manage the tires from the start: less entry aggression and smoother steering can protect late-stint pace at 3×.
Darlington Raceway.watchFor: A fuel stretch is not a win if worn tires cost more time than the stop you avoid. Evaluate fresh-tire recovery carefully.
Darlington Raceway.referenceNote: 293-lap spring reference; the Southern 500 uses 367 laps. Select the game event length before planning.

Circuit of the Americas.name: Circuit of the Americas
Circuit of the Americas.preferredLine: Link late apexes to strong straightaway exits; protect grip through the slower corners and rapid direction changes.
Circuit of the Americas.savingGuidance: Coast before the heaviest braking zones and limit unnecessary throttle bursts between closely spaced turns.
Circuit of the Americas.watchFor: The reference is the 2026 2.40-mile NASCAR layout. Verify the game layout before treating lap estimates as exact.
Circuit of the Americas.referenceNote: Real-world reference; 50% lap estimate may differ from the game. Confirm the in-game race length and layout.

World Wide Technology Raceway.name: World Wide Technology Raceway
World Wide Technology Raceway.preferredLine: Treat Turns 1–2 and 3–4 separately. Use controlled braking, clean rotation, and a strong exit at each end.
World Wide Technology Raceway.savingGuidance: Lift before the heavier braking end and keep the car settled. Compare the effect on both brake demand and fuel use.
World Wide Technology Raceway.watchFor: This is Gateway in Madison, Illinois, not Atlanta. Protect tires and brakes while managing its unequal corner shapes.
World Wide Technology Raceway.referenceNote: Real-world reference; 50% lap estimate may differ from the game. Confirm the in-game race length and layout.

Martinsville Speedway.name: Martinsville Speedway
Martinsville Speedway.preferredLine: Use a patient low-line entry, rotate without excessive steering, and maximize exit traction.
Martinsville Speedway.savingGuidance: Lift before braking and apply throttle progressively. Rear-wheel spin is a poor trade for a brief straightaway gain.
Martinsville Speedway.watchFor: Do not extend a fuel run past useful rear-tire life. Braking discipline and pit-road execution matter.
Martinsville Speedway.referenceNote: 400-lap spring reference; the fall race uses 500 laps. Confirm the game event length.
